card_title: 3 Questions to Ask Before You Pick an AI Tool
card_desc: A 15-minute worksheet: find the task worth handing to AI, define what done looks like, and check what you already pay for before you buy anything.
meta_title: 3 Questions to Ask Before You Pick an AI Tool (Free Worksheet) | Olivia Porter
meta_description: A free worksheet to answer before you buy another AI tool: find the task that eats your week, write what done looks like, and check what you already pay for. With copy-and-paste prompts.
sub: Pick the task first. Then the tool. Here are the 3 questions I ask before anyone buys an AI tool, as a worksheet you can fill in.
intro: Most people start with the tool: they see a demo, buy it, and then go looking for something to use it on. That's backwards.
Start with the task. Answer these 3 questions in order and you'll know exactly what to hand to AI, what good looks like, and whether you even need to buy anything.

before.label: Before you start
items: Grab a doc or a notebook. You'll write a few short answers and paste them into the prompts below.
Don't skip to question 3. The tool only makes sense once you know the task and the finish line.

sections.label: Question 1
sections.title: Which task eats the most hours in your week?

steps.title: Track one week
steps.text: If you're not sure where your time goes, write it down for one week: the task, how long it took, and how often you did it. Rough is fine.

steps.title: Score your top 5
steps.text: Take your 5 biggest tasks and score each one from 1 to 5 on these. The highest total is your best first task for AI.
list: Hours: how much of your week it takes.
Repeat: how often you do it the same way.
Steps: could you write them down for someone else?
Low risk: how easy is a mistake to catch and fix? (Easier scores higher.)

steps.title: Or let AI sort it for you
steps.text: Paste your week into Claude or ChatGPT with this:
steps.prompt: Here's how I spent my week: [paste your list]. Group it into tasks and total the hours for each. Rank the top 5 by hours. Then score each one from 1 to 5 on how repetitive it is, how clear the steps are, and how low the risk of a mistake is. Tell me which one to hand to AI first and why.

sections.label: Question 2
sections.title: What does done look like for that task?

steps.title: Write the finish line
steps.text: Be specific. Fill in these 4 lines for the task you picked:
list: What goes in: the notes, files or data it starts from.
What comes out: the exact thing you want at the end (an email, a report, an updated record).
Who checks it: the person who signs off before it goes anywhere.
How you'll know it worked: the time it saves, or the mistake it stops.

steps.title: Here's an example
steps.text: Task: every Monday, turn last week's sales calls into a pipeline update for the team. In: call notes and the CRM. Out: a one-page summary of deals that moved and deals that are stuck. Checked by: me. It worked if: it takes 10 minutes instead of an hour.

sections.label: Question 3
sections.title: What do you already pay for that could do it?

steps.title: List what you already have
steps.text: Before you buy anything new, look at what you're already paying for. A lot of these have AI built in now.
list: Your email, calendar and meeting tools

steps.title: Ask AI to check it for you
steps.text: Paste your answers from questions 1 and 2 into this:
steps.prompt: Here's the task I want help with: [task]. Here's what done looks like: [your 4 lines]. Here are the tools I already pay for: [list]. Tell me which of these could do this today, what I'd need to set up, and what's missing. Only if nothing I have can do it, tell me what kind of tool to look for.

steps.title: If you still need something new
steps.text: Only buy it if you can say yes to all 4:
list: It works with the tools you already use, especially your CRM.
You can try it on your real task before you pay.
You know who on your team owns it and checks its work.
You can get your data out if you leave.

closing: Pick the task first. Then the tool.
